To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the interaction between the N- and C-terminus is important for the function of SK3 channels.
the N-C interaction is important for SK3 function and that this interaction is independent of the length and the number of glutamines in the N- terminus.
the N-C interaction influences SK3 channel function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interactions of N-terminal and C-terminal parts in SK3.
the interactions between the different domains of SK3 channels and their influence on the channel function.
the function of the N- and C- terminal part of the Ca2+ activated SK3 K+ channel in the regulation of the afterhyperpolorization in neurons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SK channels are tetrameric proteins and the C-terminal part of SK3 interacts with the N-terminally located part of SK3.
the interaction between N and C terminus is not only a static interaction but that the interaction is also modulating the channel activity in response to the physiological stimuli.
N-C interactions of SK3 channels modulate SK3 channel function and therefore may play a role in the modulation of the afterhyperpolorization in the nervous system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the N-C and N- N interactions are important for the function of SK channels.
SK3 channel function is influenced by N-C interactions.
the N- and C-terminus are important for the function of SK3 channels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
N-C interactions are a novel regulatory mechanism of Ca2+-activated potassium channels.
N-terminal parts of SK channels influence the function of SK channels in a Ca2+-dependent manner.
N-C interactions are important for the function of SK3.
